focus: Cross-check the router, presentation asset and check/align/apply workflows against engine flags and apply/rollback behavior.
answeredQuestions: Q3: Do update.md and doctor-update-presentation.txt meet the sk-create-command contract (thin router, presentation split, approval gates, dry-run, rollback), and do they agree with the workflows?

label: A hard process termination can strand .skilled/release/.apply.lock: apply writes rollback.json before target writes and removes the lock only in finally, while rollback must acquire the same exclusive lock and refuses when it already exists. The workflow says to leave a pre-existing lock untouched. Existing tests cover a recoverable write exception and a separately held lock, not process death. The hard-kill consequence is inferred from the control flow; add stale-owner recovery or an explicit recovery procedure and a process-termination test.

The align and apply workflow command templates advertise --include-prerelease, but their user_inputs blocks do not declare include_prerelease. The router accepts it and the engine parser supports it, so the workflow has no declared field to bind; unless runtime binding bypasses user_inputs, prerelease selection cannot reach the engine through these actions. Add the missing input declarations and an align/apply latest-prerelease case.

The router's presentation boundary says all visible wording lives in doctor-update-presentation.txt, but its workflow summary also gives first-run base-recording instructions. The presentation asset already owns the complete baseRecording prompt. This duplicates next-step wording in the router and conflicts with the sk-create-command ownership rule.
